This is a classic pigeonhole principle: if we have more pigeons than holes, then at least one hole must contain more than one pigeon. The condition "each hole contains at most one pigeon" means it's impossible to place 18 pigeons into 17 holes without at least one hole having two pigeons. Therefore, this is unsatisfiable.
